- Earlier rounds' significant results: iter_0 min-rule member rate, shared-last-digit nonmember; iter_1 outside-minus-inside range (people stay inside the range more), fewer intermediate cells.

- iter_2 cand_4 (parity_restricted_concepts): incumbent + odd/even-restricted copies of every rule & interval (prior share rho, MAP ~0.2) — MAP logp -1470 vs incumbent MAP -1477. Incumbent's biggest residuals: even targets for all-odd sets (63,27,99,33→42; 23,35,95,83→34) predicted ~0.33, observed 0; 98,83→8/28 overpredicted. Parity restriction helps only modestly.
- iter_3 critique (incumbent parity_restricted_concepts) new stats: partial-last-digit majority (69,9,39,21 → x9 high), monotone presentation order in 3-ex shared-digit sets (62,32,22 & 73,33,3 ~0.27 vs 63,23,43 ~0.05), opposite-parity multiples in 2-ex sets (7,63 even mult7 ~0.46), contains-digit-only sets (98,83; 13,91 low), range-boundary step, far opposite-parity floor, broad-rule in-range ceiling (~0.55), any-digit overlap. Check iter_3 ppc_results.json for which hit.
- iter_3 monotone-order critique is really a decade effect: 62,32,22 → 20s targets ~0.25 and 73,33,3 → 30s ~0.3 (an example sits in the target's decade), vs 63,23,43 → 30s ~0.05 (no example in that decade). Exception: 78,48,88 → 80s ~0.02. iter_3 cand_1 (place_value_context_exemplar: context-model multiplicative similarity on tens digit, units digit, parity, magnitude; 6 params) smoke-fit in-sample loglik -1551 — on par with the best concept-learning models.
- iter_3 cand_4 (orderly_list_weak_sampling): incumbent parity_restricted_concepts + evidence exponent scaled by exp(order_shift) for 3+-example sets in sorted order. - iter_3 cand_5 (monotone_order_range_prior_shift): serial_position model + prior log-odds shift (kappa) rules→intervals for sets of >=3 examples shown strictly sorted (9 such sets, e.g. 62,32,22; 73,33,3; 4,66,78,96). - iter_3 cand_2 (seriation_primed_range_concepts): incumbent + interval-family prior boost for sorted 3+-example sets; MAP loglik -1411.9 vs incumbent -1417.5 (boost ~1.4). - iter_3 cand_3 (orderly_list_discounted_evidence): incumbent + beta*exp(-delta) for sorted lists of >=3 examples. MAP logp -1460.9 vs incumbent -1470.1 (delta~0.58). Alternative (sorted list shifts prior toward intervals) only -1467.3.
- iter_3 cand_0 (ordered_sweep_concepts): incumbent + "ordered sweep" intervals (sorted lists n!/2 more likely, shuffled impossible; share kappa~Beta(1,3)). Smoke in-sample loglik -1424.6 (vs incumbent MAP -1470). The monotone-order effect rests on only 62,32,22 & 73,33,3 (71,31,21 has only target 100). check_candidate takes ~10+ min: run it in the background with timeout >= 30 min.
- iter_4 critique (incumbent monotone_order_range_prior_shift, NO parity restriction) stats: digit-only vs arithmetic-only targets (8,80,48: 28/68 .83 vs 96 .22; obs +0.18), shared-digit nonmember inside-minus-outside range (unsorted, obs -0.02), sorted-minus-unsorted out-of-range (obs +0.16, tests kappa side effect), in-range opposite-parity (obs -0.35), rule-member out-minus-in range (obs -0.19), parity 4-ex minus 3-ex (obs -0.13; 4,66,78,96 evens only ~.6), within-set target SD, shared-digit nonmember late-minus-early. Check iter_4 ppc_results.json.
- iter_4 cand_2 (extrapolation_verification_failure): incumbent monotone_order_range_prior_shift × exp(-rate*decades outside [min,max]), failed check → "no". Targets critique rule_member_out_minus_in_range (obs -0.19 vs null -0.12: people extend rules LESS outside the range; critique prose says the opposite — trust z sign). Raw yes rate of non-example targets by decades outside range: 0:.40, 1:.25, 2:.34, 3+:~.2-.28 — weak gradient overall. Check OK, smoke in-sample loglik -1419.1 (~2 min per 100/100 chain).
- iter_4 critique of monotone_order_range_prior_shift: only rule_member_out_minus_in_range hit (obs -0.19 < null -0.12: people are MORE range-confined for rule members, despite the description's wording); no stat survives FDR. Next: shared-digit in-minus-out (z -1.87), in-range opposite parity (z -1.62).
- iter_4 cand_3 (parity_conjoined_order_shift): incumbent + parity-restricted copies of rules/intervals (rho). 43 sets, 7737 concepts, pos_ll (43,4,7737).
- iter_4 cand_1 (log_number_line_ranges): best model + intervals on log(n+c) mental number line (example density ∝ psych width, W = f(b+.5)-f(a-.5); log_c ~ N(2,1.5)). Raw data: targets above examples' range yes .34 (n=414) vs below .23 (n=459) — consistent with upward-asymmetric generalization (confounded by set).
- iter_4 cand_0 (predictive_output_probability_readout): tempered_size_principle_independent but "yes" = sigmoid(slope*(log(100*posterior-predictive sample prob of target) - criterion)) instead of membership. Smoke in-sample loglik -1453.7 (vs best smoke ~-1427); check took ~3 min. Targets the iter_4 rule-member out-minus-in-range critique (obs -0.19 vs null -0.12).
- iter_4 cand_4 (refining monotone_order_range_prior_shift, incumbent MAP observed loglik -1410.4): decade-bounded rules (rule ∩ [10a+1,10b], share rho) only -1409.6; 5-step bounds → rho→0 (no gain). Grafting parity-restricted concepts (parity_conjoined_order_shift) -1409.1, rho~0.17. The rule_member_out_minus_in_range critique is mostly parity: 69,9,39,21's out-of-range multiples of 3 (72-96) are even. Gains from new concept families are now ~1 nat at MAP — the concept-learning family looks saturated.
- iter_4 critique: rule_member_out_minus_in_range observed -0.19 vs null -0.12 (people confine rule members to the example range MORE than model; the stat's description text has the direction backwards). Only raw p, q=0.18. iter_4 cand_5 (range_bounded_parity_concepts): parity_restricted_concepts + rule∩covering-range concepts (share eta, scatter-sum trick from bounded_range_rule_learning; 644k hyps over 43 sets). check_candidate OK, smoke in-sample loglik -1433.6, 1-chain 200 iters took ~6.5 min.
  Smoke-fit in-sample loglik -1425.4 (incumbent smoke -1427: little gain); check ~9 min.
- iter_4 cand_4 repair (range_bounded_rules_order_shift): first attempt parity_conjoined_order_shift was rejected as an exact duplicate (RMSE 0) of a model already admitted under that name — check models/ for same-mechanism files before resubmitting. Repair = incumbent + rule∩covering-range concepts (share eta of rule prior, per-position hyp ll so serial weighting applies; shift = Σ pos_w·per-position max upper bound).
- iter_4 cand_5 repair (range_bounded_parity_concepts): first attempt rejected as too slow (644k-hyp scatter). Fix: group covering-range bounded rules by (rule, size) per set (same likelihood within a group → 601 slots/set with log-count + mean membership), compute unbounded part as one dense (sets×H)@(H×100) dot then gather cells, bounded part per asked cell (280 cells). Gradient eval ~47 ms (vs ~120+ ms). Perf lessons: per-cell gathers of wide rows (7737) and broadcast-multiply (sets×601×100) are slow in the gradient; dense dot + index is fast. pm initial_point is jittered — don't compare two modules' p_yes at separate initial points.

# Critique of `consistent_examples_bounded_rules`

2 of 8 evaluated test statistics show a significant discrepancy (p ≤ 0.05), over 1000 posterior-predictive replicates.

## Significant discrepancies (a better model should address these)

Raw two-sided p shown with a Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted q across this round's statistics. Prioritise discrepancies that survive the FDR (`q ≤ alpha`); a raw-only hit may be one of several screened at once.
- **ruleless_set_in_range_rate** — On 2+ example sets that no rule (odd/even, multiples 3-12, powers, squares, cubes, primes, ends-in/contains digit) fits fully, yes rate for in-range non-example targets; observed above null means the model under-endorses the range when no rule explains every example (too much belief kept on near-fitting rules). (observed 0.489 vs null mean 0.403, z=4.07, p=0.002, q=0.016) [survives FDR]
- **in_minus_out_range_two_examples** — On 2-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' range minus yes rate for targets outside it; observed above null means the model under-weights range/interval generalization relative to rules for pairs. (observed 0.204 vs null mean 0.14, z=2.88, p=0.00599, q=0.024) [survives FDR]

"""Refinement of consistent_examples_bounded_rules: ranges get their own evidence strength.

People do the same tempered, sample-size-neglecting Bayesian concept learning as
the incumbent (45 weighted rules, intervals with a prior proportional to
size ** size_power, odd/even versions, range-bounded rules that every example
fits; digit and bounded rules discounted for one-example sets). The one change:
people weigh the examples as evidence differently depending on the kind of
concept. A magnitude range ("numbers between 40 and 60") is judged with its own
evidence strength, shifted from the strength used for mathematical and digit
rules by an inferred amount (range_evidence_shift; 0 recovers the incumbent).

selected, which changes the balance of in-range against out-of-range

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),

    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


def log_lik_table(membership):
    size = membership.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    in_part = np.where(size > 0, ALPHA * membership / np.maximum(size, 1), 0.0)
    return np.log(in_part + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)

    uniq, counts = np.unique(rows, axis=0, return_counts=True)
    return uniq, counts.astype("float64")


_RULES = rule_concepts()

BASE_RULE = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES], dtype="float64")
BASE_INT = np.array([(NUMBERS >= m) & (NUMBERS <= n) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)], dtype="float64")

    members of a group share prior and likelihood, so each is summarised by its
    log count, log-likelihood and mean membership of every target."""

    out = []

        w = INT_COUNT[sel]

    b_mem = np.zeros((n, hb, 100))

        for j, (r, ln, ll, mem) in enumerate(g):

        "interval_log_count": i_logn,
        "interval_log_lik": i_ll,
        "bounded_rule": b_rule,
        "bounded_log_count": b_logn,
        "bounded_log_lik": b_ll,
        "single_example": np.array([1.0 if len(s) == 1 else 0.0 for s in unique]),
        "centered_log_n": np.log(np.array([len(s) for s in unique], dtype="float64") / 2.0),
        "row_cell": np.array([cell_index[c] for c in cell_keys], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }


with pm.Model() as model:
    cell_set = pm.Data("cell_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cell_membership = pm.Data("cell_membership", np.zeros((1, 3)))
    rule_log_lik = pm.Data("rule_log_lik", np.zeros((1, 3 * N_RULES)))
    interval_family = pm.Data("interval_family", np.zeros((1, 1), dtype="int64"))
    interval_log_size = pm.Data("interval_log_size", np.zeros((1, 1)))
    interval_log_count = pm.Data("interval_log_count", np.zeros((1, 1)))
    interval_log_lik = pm.Data("interval_log_lik", np.zeros((1, 1)))
    bounded_rule = pm.Data("bounded_rule", np.zeros((1, 1), dtype="int64"))
    bounded_log_count = pm.Data("bounded_log_count", np.zeros((1, 1)))
    bounded_log_lik = pm.Data("bounded_log_lik", np.zeros((1, 1)))
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    centered_log_n = pm.Data("centered_log_n", np.zeros(1))
    single_example = pm.Data("single_example", np.zeros(1))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    set_weights = pm.Dirichlet("set_weights", a=SET_CONCENTRATION)
    zero_split = pm.Beta("zero_split", 2, 2)
    shared = set_weights[END_0]
    rule_weights = pm.Deterministic("rule_weights", pt.concatenate([
        set_weights[:END_0], (zero_split * shared)[None], set_weights[END_0 + 1:CONTAINS_0],
        ((1 - zero_split) * shared)[None], set_weights[CONTAINS_0:],
    ]))
    log_beta = pm.Normal("log_beta", mu=0.0, sigma=0.75)
    neglect = pm.Normal("neglect", 0.0, 0.5)
    beta = pt.exp(log_beta - neglect * centered_log_n)[:, None]
    # The one change: magnitude ranges get their own (shifted) evidence strength.
    range_evidence_shift = pm.Normal("range_evidence_shift", mu=0.0, sigma=1.0)
    beta_range = pt.exp(log_beta + range_evidence_shift - neglect * centered_log_n)[:, None]
    rho = pm.Beta("rho", 1.0, 3.0)  # parity-restricted share
    eta = pm.Beta("eta", 1.0, 3.0)  # range-bounded share of the rule prior
    # Interval prior proportional to size ** size_power, normalised per family.
    size_power = pm.Normal("size_power", mu=0.0, sigma=1.0)
    fam = pt.stack([pt.log1p(-rho), pt.log(rho / 2), pt.log(rho / 2)])
    log_z = pt.logsumexp(size_power * LOG_SIZE_GRID[None, :] + np.log(FAM_SIZE_COUNT + 1e-300), axis=1)
    log_w = pt.log(rule_weights)

    log_int = (pt.log1p(-lambda_0) + fam[interval_family] - log_z[interval_family]

    log_bounded = (pt.log(lambda_0) + pt.log(eta) - np.log(N_INT) + log_w[bounded_rule]
                   + bounded_log_count + beta * bounded_log_lik)
    comparison_neglect = pm.HalfNormal("comparison_neglect", sigma=3.0)
    pen = comparison_neglect * single_example[:, None]
    # Bounded rules (defined by the examples' span) are also discounted for one example.

    full = pt.concatenate([log_rule_prior[None, :] - pen * DIGIT3[None, :] + beta * rule_log_lik, log_int, log_bounded], axis=1)

    in_concept = (posterior[cell_set] * cell_membership).sum(axis=1)

    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(in_concept[row_cell], 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)
